name: Event Organization Portal - SIA Project 21 22
description:
Information Systems - academic year 21/22
Course Project
Version 1.0.1 - 20/12/2021
Consider the following scenario:

A startup intends to develop a web portal that can help people who intend to organize an event, bringing together in a single website the information concerning the guests and the various services necessary for the event itself to take place.

The platform to be developed envisages the presence of providers and guests, in addition to the organizer.

At registration, providers supply, in addition to their credentials, their personal data and the data of the company they manage (VAT number, company address, accepted payment methods).

The provider, once registered, will be able to enter the services offered by their company, each belonging to a category (catering, hairdresser, florist etc.), each of which will be associated with a virtual showcase in which the provider can upload demonstration photos, together with the corresponding prices and the hours corresponding to the particular service shown by the showcase (e.g. Hairdresser's blow-dry service has as hours 10:00-12:00 from Tuesday to Thursday, Haircut + shampoo service with hours 8:00-12:00 + 15:00-18:00 from Tuesday to Saturday).

The event organizer, identified by their tax code, at registration, in addition to choosing their credentials, will provide their personal data, residence data and their IBAN for the possible payment of the services.

The organizer, through the portal, will be able to create the event, choosing the type of event (wedding, graduation, concert…) to organize, the date, the place where it will be held and the budget planned for the organization of the event. When creating the event the organizer will be able to choose from a pre-existing list the types of service for which they are interested in receiving help (for example catering, flowers, taxi service etc.).

The organizer will also be able to add the guests to the portal, entering the corresponding data, specifying, in addition to the personal data, the email with which the guest will be identified (and which they will use to log in) and the category to which the guest belongs (relative, friend, colleague etc.).

For each guest added, the system will generate an invitation code that will be sent by email to the specified address; this code will be used by the guest as a password to access the portal.

The organizer will also have available a blog associated with their event in which the organizer or the guests can write information about the event, post photos or videos and leave their thoughts by creating new posts or commenting on the existing ones.

The organizer, once the event has been created, will be able to view, for each service chosen when creating the event, the showcases of the providers that supply the chosen type of service and to arrange an appointment compatible with the hours observed by that service, specifying the details and any special requests. The provider, through their interface, will be able to view the various appointment requests and will have to approve them. The approved requests are displayed directly in a calendar on the site associated with the event, where the organizer will be able to consult the appointments for the agreed services.

After the meeting between the provider and the organizer (in which they agree on the details of the service), the provider calculates the quotation and proceeds to upload the amount on the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once the upload has taken place the organizer can choose whether to accept or reject the quotation; if it is accepted, the total amount is subtracted from the remaining budget. By accepting the amount, the organizer chooses the payment mode (instalments, deposit + balance or full amount) and the payment method (online or on site). If the payment takes place on site the provider will proceed to confirm the amount paid through the portal (in the case of payment in several instalments the provider confirms the amount of each instalment received).

At any time the organizer will be able to consult the history of the contracts (with the related status and cost) and the budget balance for the entire event.
highLevelGoals: The Event Organizer aims to efficiently create, configure, and manage all aspects of their events, including event type, date, location, and budget, through a centralized web portal.
The Event Organizer seeks to easily add and manage guest information, categorize guests, and facilitate secure invitation delivery and access to event details for their invited attendees.
The Event Organizer desires to discover and book suitable services for their event from a diverse range of providers, ensuring compatibility with event requirements and budget.
The Event Organizer aims to maintain clear visibility over event expenditures, manage quotations, and track the remaining budget and payment statuses for all contracted services.

The Event Organizer wants to foster communication and collaboration among guests and themselves through an integrated event blog, allowing for information sharing, photo/video uploads, and discussions.
The Provider aims to effectively showcase their services, including demonstration photos, pricing, and availability, to attract potential Event Organizers and secure bookings.
The Provider seeks to efficiently manage appointment requests, approve bookings, generate quotations, and track payment confirmations for services rendered.
The Provider desires a secure platform to manage their company details, accepted payment methods, and service-specific information, ensuring accuracy and accessibility.
The Guest aims to easily access relevant information about the event they are invited to, including details shared by the Event Organizer.
The Guest desires to actively participate in the event's blog by creating posts, commenting on existing content, and sharing photos or videos related to the event.
lowLevelGoals: The Event Organizer can initiate the creation of a new event by providing basic details.
The Event Organizer can select a predefined event type or input a custom one.
The Event Organizer can input the start and end dates and times for the event.
The Event Organizer can input the physical address and name of the event venue.
The Event Organizer can set the total allocated budget for the event.
The Event Organizer can choose from a pre-existing list of service categories (e.g., catering, photography) when creating an event to filter subsequent provider searches.
The Event Organizer can modify any previously entered event information.
The Event Organizer can access a dashboard or list displaying all events they have organized.
The Event Organizer can consult a calendar displaying all approved service appointments for a specific event.
The Event Organizer can input a guest's name, email, and other relevant contact details.
The Event Organizer can group guests based on custom or predefined categories.
The Event Organizer can trigger the sending of email invitations containing a unique access code to guests.
The Event Organizer can modify existing guest records.
The Event Organizer can delete a guest's record from the event's guest list.
The Event Organizer can navigate through different types of services offered by providers.
The Event Organizer can access a provider's page showing their services, portfolio, reviews, and contact information.
The Event Organizer can send a request to a provider for an appointment, specifying desired date, time, and any special requirements, ensuring compatibility with the provider's availability.
The Event Organizer can send a request to a provider for a price estimate for their services.
The Event Organizer can confirm and finalize the booking of a service with a provider.
The Event Organizer can see all services they have contracted for a particular event, including contract status and cost history.
The Event Organizer can input details of a cost incurred for the event.
The Event Organizer can access a report showing all recorded costs.
The Event Organizer can accept or decline a quotation for services.
The Event Organizer can select how and when to pay for a service after accepting a quotation.
The Event Organizer can view the current budget balance after accounting for expenditures and booked services.
The Event Organizer can publish new content, announcements, or updates to the event's blog.
The Event Organizer can attach multimedia files to their blog entries.
The Event Organizer can reply to guest comments on their blog entries.
The Event Organizer can modify the content of their previously published blog posts.
The Event Organizer can remove a blog post from the event's blog.
The Provider can add a new service to their profile, specifying its characteristics.
The Provider can add visual media to illustrate their service offerings.
The Provider can define the cost structure for their services.
The Provider can specify recurring time slots and days of the week when their service is available.
The Provider is alerted when an Event Organizer requests an appointment.
The Provider can access the specific details and special requests made by an Event Organizer for an appointment.
The Provider can accept or reject a proposed appointment time.
The Provider can create and send a formal price estimate to an Event Organizer.
The Provider can monitor the responses to their sent quotations.
The Provider is alerted when an Event Organizer confirms payment for a service.
The Provider can actively confirm and record the payment amount received for a service, especially for partial payments or instalments.
The Provider can modify their business's general information.
The Provider can specify which payment options they support for their services.
The Provider can add or edit details unique to each service they offer.
The Guest can view a list of all events they have been invited to.
The Guest can use the invitation code sent via email as a password to access the event portal.
The Guest can see all the core information about an event.
The Guest can read any new information or changes posted by the organizer.
The Guest can browse all posts and content on the event's dedicated blog.
The Guest can publish their own content to the event's blog.
The Guest can add their thoughts or replies to any blog entry.
The Guest can share multimedia content related to the event.
